=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Context:** Baseline is 100% of Paperbark Analytics for AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. The Seller's cover note calls its positions "FINAL" and says they were "settled at principal level." That label doesn't bind Wattlebridge and shouldn't shape our response. Its market claims (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month limitation periods) are the Seller's assertions and should be tested against our own precedent and market data.

**Key exposure point:** The Seller's own disclosures identify known items totalling about AUD 4.13m: Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k, and Sandbar AUD 330k. Clause 8.3 would bar buyer claims for any matter we know about, and we now know about all of these. Unless we obtain specific indemnities or price adjustments, the Seller's draft leaves us with almost no recourse for them. The privacy incident and Bluefen revenue risk are unquantified and sit on top of that.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** General warranty claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at 100% of price for general warranties as an opening position, with a fallback set by the deal team. Fundamental, tax and specific indemnities sit outside this cap (see N-004, N-014).
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%. It is the Seller's number, not a market standard we have verified, and it would leave the known AUD 4.13m items largely uncovered.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis per claim; AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (around AUD 10k) with related claims aggregated, so a series of small related claims (e.g., privacy) isn't defeated one by one. A tipping basket at around 0.5% (about AUD 120k), so once it is crossed we recover from the first dollar. Basket and de minimis should not apply to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A deductible basket at this level, combined with a per-claim de minimis, would absorb a large share of realistic warranty losses.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General warranty claims notifiable within 18 months of Completion. Any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties, so they cover at least one full audit and tax cycle. Fundamental and tax claims run to the statutory limitation period (6 years for contract claims under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW), to be confirmed). Specific indemnities run for their own stated periods.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the blanket "applies to all Claims" language. Each category needs its own period.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties are subject to the general cap and time limits.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, capacity, authority and share-ownership warranties capped at the full price, outside the basket and de minimis, with a 6-year (or statute) period. Disclosure and buyer knowledge should not apply to them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the core asset we are buying, and it should not be subject to the same limits as operational warranties.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Silent on fraud. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud claims are not subject to caps, baskets, time limits, disclosure or non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** Require an express fraud carve-out. As drafted, the "all Claims" wording could be read to cover fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 deem disclosure of everything in the data room (to 22 Sept 2026), the accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** No general data-room disclosure. Only specific, fairly disclosed items in the Disclosure Letter qualify warranties. The data room is a stale snapshot and needs a bring-down to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. General disclosure of the whole data room would effectively remove most warranty protection.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. At most, limit it to the actual knowledge of named individuals, with no imputed or constructive knowledge. Known issues must be covered by specific indemnities, which clause 8.3 must expressly not override.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3. It would bar claims for the very issues we have already identified in diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Change-control consent (cl. 11.2, with conditions in 11.3) is "addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. No final consent is in the data room. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Written Bluefen consent in agreed form, with the clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. An absolute obligation to obtain it, not reasonable endeavours. A walk right, or a price adjustment, if it isn't obtained.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "reasonable endeavours" and "deemed satisfied." Make it a condition precedent, because losing ~30% of revenue is a value-level risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release to be provided after Completion. Not repaid, and no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Payoff at Completion under a payoff letter, with the security discharged and the PPSR registrations removed. The payoff is funded from the price as a debt item under our debt-free/cash-free basis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. We should not take on a AUD 3.2m secured facility and hope for a release later.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). Not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and any other employment taxes), treated as seller-borne debt-like items deducted from the price and included in the funds flow.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as debt-like. Amounts owed because of a Seller-driven transaction should not fall to the Company after Completion. The on-cost figure still needs to be quantified.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. AUD 180k is open. No receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims and IP ownership, not just the SOW3 payment. Pre-Completion payment of the AUD 180k, or a retention. A confirmatory assignment of all Project Materials as a Completion deliverable. Outside basket, de minimis and clause 8.3.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity. Our ownership of the core IP is not assured until the payment and assignment are delivered.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 export of ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. Scope and access unknown. Notification status unknown. The Seller calls it "not expected to be material" and states no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity for all losses from the incident, including investigation and forensic costs, notification costs, regulatory action, and third-party claims. Outside the cap, basket and clause 8.3. A completed forensic investigation before Completion, or a dedicated retention or escrow. Privacy-law analysis (the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) may apply if the Company is an APP entity, which needs confirming).
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific indemnity plus a dedicated retention. The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported by any loss figure or completed investigation.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k, described as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure doesn't say whether they are terminable, accrued or unavoidable.
- **Buyer wants:** A schedule of each renewal showing term, termination rights and whether it is committed beyond Completion. Confirmation of whether they overlap or are staggered, since the disclosure asks us to read them together. Any commitment outside the ordinary course, or beyond Completion without the buyer's consent, to be treated as a seller cost or debt-like item. Interim covenant not to renew without consent.
- **Recommendation:** Accept only once a schedule confirms the renewals are ordinary-course and terminable. Otherwise treat them as debt-like.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime for everything (cap, basket, time limit, disclosure, knowledge).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority), (c) tax, (d) IP, and (e) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, lease, Mossvale). Each category has its own cap, time limit and exclusions.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A single regime makes the known issues and the fundamental warranties subject to the weakest general terms.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of shares. Doesn't state that the buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing or Completion: current ASIC company extract, the register of members, the share transfer documents, a PPSR search over the shares, and a review of the constitution for transfer restrictions or pre-emptive rights. Title warranties should be fundamental (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Verify independently. A share register supplied by the Seller is a starting point, not proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime." No separate tax indemnity.
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity with its own period (statute). Full tax warranties. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, open-source use and employee/contractor assignment, with IP treated as a fundamental-type item for the core platform.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Pre-Completion tax liabilities and IP ownership are not appropriate for the general regime, and the Ironquay and bonus items already show exposure in these areas.

---

**Next steps:**
1. Confirm the NSW limitation periods and any privacy-law analysis with NSW counsel.
2. Engage tax advisers on the bonus on-costs, pre-Completion tax indemnity, and any payroll tax exposure.
3. Request the Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay documents and the Sandbar schedule, and run the ASIC and PPSR searches (N-015).
4. Bring the data room down to the current date, since the disclosure cut-off is 22 Sept 2026 and today is 5 Nov 2026.

This is a first-pass review of the Seller's draft and disclosure letter. It is not a full SPA review, and the specific positions need sign-off by the deal team and NSW counsel before we respond to the Seller.
